claims.price_target: $3-8/bbl structural premium at Sunday CME open — target $75-80/bbl
claims.strategy: Long crude — fade-the-move on Sunday gap (65% win rate for geopolitical structural changes). OPEC+ 188k bpd dip is an additional entry opportunity.
claims.crowd_belief: Markets price Iran as 'contained skirmishing.' Polymarket has no active contract for Hormuz toll scenario. OPEC+ increase seen as bearish.
claims.contradiction: The $1.5-2M/tanker toll is NOT a skirmish — it's a structural change in global oil transit cost that the market has zero history pricing. OPEC+'s 188k bpd is a rounding error vs. daily Hormuz toll revenue extraction.

claims.price_target: +10-20% on shipping rate re-pricing as Hormuz risk premium loads into contracts
claims.strategy: Long tanker shipping — Hormuz toll turns into war risk premium for shipping lines. Every tanker that transits Hormuz now carries a $1.5-2M cost that gets passed to cargo rates.
claims.crowd_belief: Tanker rates not yet pricing Hormuz structural change. Shipping analysts still focused on OPEC+ supply dynamics.
claims.contradiction: The Hormuz toll is a direct transfer from global oil trade to Iran. Tanker companies that transit Hormuz will either pay (cost passed to rates) or divert around Africa (massively higher cost). Either path = tanker rate spike.

claims.strategy: Long gold as geopolitical hedge — multi-front escalation (Hormuz toll + Beirut strikes + Kuwait strikes + Taiwan patrol) creates compounding safe-haven demand.
claims.crowd_belief: Gold at $2,415 reflects elevated Middle East risk, but the escalation has gone from one front to three (Iran-Kuwait, Iran-Hormuz, Israel-Beirut). This compounding is not priced.
claims.contradiction: Each front independently justifies gold — combined they create a safe-haven demand spike that exceeds any single-front pricing. Gold remains the cleanest cross-theater geopolitical hedge.

claims.price_target: -3-5% at Monday Asia open if Taiwan tension escalates
claims.strategy: Short / put options — China extended maritime patrols east of Taiwan while US is Middle East-distracted. Strategic opportunism thesis.
claims.crowd_belief: Markets focused on Middle East entirely. Taiwan risk premium near zero. Consensus: 'China won't invade Taiwan this cycle.'
claims.contradiction: China extends patrols east of Taiwan exactly when US is locked into a multi-front Middle East war — textbook strategic opportunism. The Taiwan risk premium is underpriced vs. reality.

claims.strategy: Short duration bonds — oil spike feeds inflation expectations, Fed less likely to cut. Stagflation regime favors commodities over bonds.
claims.crowd_belief: Markets fully priced Fed rate hike by end-2026. 2-year real yields at Trump-era highs. But oil structural change from Hormuz toll compounds already-hawkish bond pricing.
claims.contradiction: The market has priced a rate hike but NOT the compounding effect of a structural oil cost increase on inflation expectations. The bond selloff has further to go.
